I view AI not as a threat to human creativity but as a profound evolution of our tools for expression. Imagine if we had “un-invented” photography because it changed painting, or word processors because they transformed writing. In each case, the art didn’t disappear—it adapted, expanded, and reached new heights. AI offers a similar opportunity to deepen human creativity, not diminish it.

Far from making human effort pointless, collaboration with AI can help us explore uncharted creative territories, express ideas we didn’t know we could, and even reimagine what it means to be an artist. The heart of art—its emotion, meaning, and connection—remains uniquely human. With AI as a creative partner, we’re not losing our place in the creative process—we’re gaining a new perspective on what it means to create. While this shift may be difficult and even painful at times, it holds the potential to transform art and creativity into something richer, more expansive, and more inclusive than ever before. comments: I don't know where to start here. AI is still in its early stages and people are both optimistic and fearful about its potential. People are both frustrated with AI's inaccuracies and the fact that it doesn't seem to know everything from the onset of its existence. While also being fearful of its all-knowing, all-seeing Skynet people replacing, famine causing future. It all really doesn't make a whole lot of sense to me because those fears are often overblown. Especially when those in the media, that have no background in anything technological start fearmongering. It harkens back to when the Today show hosts were musing to each other "have you heard of this internet?" Ai is a tool, currently it is very helpful to me and will become more helpful in the future. It makes learning easier and more streamlined. It gives me information and places to look further to understanding the topics that I am interested in. I understand Ai's potential and have to parse the bullshit coming from people that are all shouting into the void about its negative consequences. I have to figure out which of those voices aren't just imbeciles barking nonsense and which of those are genuine inevitabilities. Nonetheless, AI is here to stay, and I will be utilizing it to the best I can. You either have to adapt to and understand the technology that controls our lives otherwise you are at a disadvantage.
